name: GA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+27 district lean makes the seat overwhelmingly Democratic
Incumbent Hank Johnson runs with a large fundraising edge over an unfunded challenger
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
No polls or expert ratings signal a competitive race
model.rationale: A D+27 district, a well-funded incumbent facing a Republican with no reported fundraising, and markets pricing a near-certain Democratic win leave no basis for expecting competition; every piece of available evidence points the same direction.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary development such as a major scandal or a late wave of outside spending against Johnson could put this seat in play, and no such signs have appeared.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 4th District sits deep in Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 27 points toward Democrats. Hank Johnson, the longtime incumbent, is running for another term and has raised nearly half a million dollars, while Republican James Duffie shows no reported fundraising. No general-election polls exist, itself a sign that neither party treats the seat as contested.

Prediction markets price Johnson's chances at about 98 percent, and no expert ratings flag the race. Districts this lean rarely fall within single digits even in strong Republican environments, and the challenger lacks the money or profile to change that. The forecast places Johnson's expected margin near 28 points, making this one of the safest Democratic House seats on the 2024 map.
